title: fix(app-shell,plugin-detail): the record page counts each comment's replies on read, and a comment with none offers the reply input (objectui#12144)
body:
Fixes #12144

Clause-②: no

On the record page's discussion, a reply stored on the server now shows under its comment, and every comment read from the server offers the reply input wherever the caller may post one.

## Measured first, on the base (`158c75d`)

The pin `RecordDetailView.replyCountOnRead-12144.test.tsx` (`@object-ui/app-shell`) renders `RecordDetailView` with no authored page. `buildDefaultPageSchema` then composes `record:discussion`, whose renderer (`record-chatter.tsx`) turns `feed.enableThreading` on. A fake data source answers the record's `sys_comment` and `sys_activity` reads, and the test drives the real panel. Run on commit `7a19eaa`, which adds only the pin to the base: `Tests  6 failed | 1 passed (7)`. The one green case is the threading-off control.

- **Effect 1 confirmed.** With one parent row and one child row read, the child is on screen nowhere. It is not a root row, and the parent has no reply-count toggle (`Unable to find an accessible element with the role "button" and name /1 reply/`).
- **Effect 2 confirmed.** No comment read from the server offers the reply input, with or without replies (`Unable to find an element with the placeholder text of: Reply…`). So the first reply on a comment cannot be posted from the page.

Cause, read on the base:
- The `sys_comment` read maps `parentId: c.parent_id` and never sets `replyCount`. Only `handleAddReply` bumps `replyCount`, and it runs only after a reply is posted through the input.
- With threading on, `RecordActivityTimeline` takes every item with a `parentId` out of the root list. It drew `ThreadedReplies`, the only place the reply list and the reply input render, only when `item.replyCount` is above zero.

## The fix

- **`@object-ui/app-shell` `RecordDetailView`.** In the same step that maps `parentId`, the `sys_comment` read counts each comment's children among the rows it returned and sets `replyCount`. This follows the platform's own contract: objectstack's `sys_comment` object definition (`plugin-audit`, `sys-comment.object.ts`) retired the stored `reply_count` and prescribes "count `parent_id` children at read time". The count groups by a truthy `parent_id` in a `Map`, the same way the timeline groups replies, so the two cannot disagree.
- **`@object-ui/plugin-detail` `RecordActivityTimeline`.** The reply input is offered on every `comment` row the host hands `onAddReply` for, with or without replies, and on no other row (module-private `canTakeReply`). The reason matches objectui#11035's `canStoreReaction`: a reply is a `sys_comment` whose parent is a comment. An activity row's id would store a comment under an activity, and no read shows it there. The reply **list** keeps its one `replyCount` gate: a row whose `replyCount` is zero is handed no replies. So whether replies show never depends on whether the caller may post one, and no second threading model is added.

No prop, export, type member or locale key is added. The two new identifiers, `canTakeReply` and `NO_REPLIES`, are module-private, so the claim's `Clause-②: no` holds.

## Dispatch hypotheses

- **H1, confirmed** on `158c75d`, by the `git grep` and reads above.
- **H2, confirmed** through the host path: the synthesized default page, the real `sys_comment` read and mapping, and the real panel. The page pin above is the measurement. A pin of the timeline alone is kept separate and is not counted as the host measurement.
- **H3, confirmed and unchanged.** `onAddReply` reaches the panel only under the `feedComment` grant (objectui#12140). With the create grant on `sys_comment`, every comment offers the input, a zero-reply comment included. With a read-only grant, no row offers it, and the stored reply still shows under its parent.
- **H4, confirmed.** The zero-reply input needed a change to the timeline's render condition, and that change fits inside the file. No new prop, export or locale key was needed, so there was no `needs_decision`.

## Pins (both new)

- `packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.replyCountOnRead-12144.test.tsx`, through the default record page, 7 cases:
  - (a) a parent and one child shows the child under the parent;
  - (a2) two children read as `2 replies`;
  - (b) under a create grant, every comment row offers the input, a zero-reply one included;
  - (b2) a `sys_activity` row offers none;
  - (b3) the first reply on a read comment posts with `parent_id` and then shows under it;
  - (d) a read-only grant gives no input, and the stored reply still shows;
  - (c) CONTROL: with threading off (an authored `record:discussion` with `feed.enableThreading: false`), the list is unchanged: three rows in read order, no toggle, no input.
- `packages/plugin-detail/src/__tests__/RecordActivityTimeline.zeroReplyInput-12144.test.tsx`, the timeline's render condition alone, 6 cases:
  - the input on a zero-reply comment, with a no-`onAddReply` control;
  - no input on an activity row;
  - a threading-off control;
  - the list's `replyCount` gate in both directions.

## Ablations (one-shot, not left in the tree)

Each mutation went through `ablation-replace.mjs`, which reports the anchor hit count, the replacement count and the blob change. Each was restored with blob equal to HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`. vitest resolves `@object-ui/plugin-detail` to `src` through the root `vitest.config.mts` alias table, so no `dist/` is in the path.

1. Read mapping without the count (`replyCount: undefined`): the page pin goes red on (a), (a2) and (d), `3 failed | 4 passed`. The input cases stay green, because the input no longer depends on the count.
2. Input re-gated on `replyCount` (the base's condition): `6 failed | 7 passed` across both pins, which is the three input cases in each file.
3. Input on every row (comment-only check removed): `2 failed | 11 passed`, the two activity-row cases.
4. List without the `replyCount` gate: `1 failed | 12 passed`, the timeline's list-gate case.

## Verification (all on `f7f477a`; `main` unmoved at `158c75d` when the PR opened)

- Dependency closure build: `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...' --filter='@object-ui/plugin-detail^...' --concurrency=2` gave `Tasks: 28 successful, 28 total`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail --filter @object-ui/app-shell run type-check`: both packages echoed `type-check` and printed `Done`. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists both new pins.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-detail/`: `Test Files  256 passed | 1 skipped (257)`, `Tests  2491 passed | 8 skipped`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/`: `Test Files  1270 passed | 1 skipped (1271)`, `Tests  12306 passed | 9 skipped`.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `pnpm check:changeset-claims`, `pnpm check:pending-changeset-literals`, `pnpm check:control-bytes`, `pnpm check:new-line-citations` and `pnpm check:phantom-deps`: all exited 0.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` on the diff answered NOT GOVERNED.
- Lint, narrowed and not the repo-wide run (CI owns that). `eslint --format json` on the four changed source files read 4 files and 0 errors. `RecordDetailView.tsx` carries 109 warnings at both base and head. The config enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions` in `eslint.config.js`), and no rule under `eslint-rules/` reads another file, so this diff cannot move the verdict on an untouched file.
- Browser: NOT MEASURED. The sibling `../objectstack` checkout in this container has no `node_modules` and no built `spec`/`cli` `dist`, so the per-agent backend cannot boot within the foreground budget. The host render above is the required measurement.

## Acceptance notes

- **A reply whose parent is not in the read.** The `sys_comment` read carries no `$top`, so it is one page of whatever size the server answers by default. A reply whose parent is not in that page counts toward no item. With threading on, it is still shown nowhere, as before. No second fetch was added.
- **The page window.** `record:discussion`'s window (`feed.limit`, default 20) takes the last N items of the merged feed, and a reply counts toward it. A reply whose parent is older than the window shows nowhere until "Load more" reaches the parent. That is the paging as it already stands, unchanged here.
- **A header comment this change falsifies.** The header of `RecordDetailView.commentWriteFailure-10899.test.tsx` says the reply writer's input "is not reachable from a loaded feed … no read sets that". That is no longer true. It is outside the claim's file surface, so it is left for the seat. The reply writer's failure path is now reachable through the page.
- **Stale docs, unchanged here.** In `content/docs/plugins/plugin-detail.mdx`, the "Console Integration" sample still uses camelCase `sys_comment` field names (`threadId`, `_id`, `author`). The `ThreadedReplies` table lists `showReplyInput`'s default as `false`, where the code defaults to `true`. Neither describes the threading this change touches, so the docs page is unchanged.

Dev session: `https://claude.ai/code/session_016djJF12Qt14ejKR5Vjt4sK` (domain:ui seat 1 dispatch, `os-dev`).
